To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
institutional trust can be a substitute for familiarity and that familiarity can be a substitute to institutional trust in interorganizational relationships.

(1) third-party institutional trust is a more effective trust mechanism in the exploration phase, whereas bilateral institutionalized trust is more effective in the maturity phase; and that (2) the underlying dimensions of trust are more effective during different phases of relationship development.

(1) third-party institutional trust is more effective than bilateral institutional trust in the initial phase of interorganizational relationship formation (2) third-party institutionalized trust is more effective for building trust in the initial phases of interorganizational relationships (3) bilateral institutionalized and familiarized trust are more effective for building interorganizational trust in the mature phases of the interorganizational relationship.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of institutional trust as the foundation of trust in online interorganiza- tional relationships, and the role of familiarity in the transition from initial to mature trust.
the development of interorganizational trust through institutional trust in online relationships.
the development of institutional trust as an initial trust-building mechanism in online inter-organizational relationship building.

institutional trust, as a substitute for familiarity, plays a significant role in the formation of interorganizational trust in online relationships.
this paper provides an important theoretical and managerial perspective on the role and nature of institutional trust in the development of online relationships.
institutional trust is a necessary and effective mechanism for building online relationships.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the institutional trust of the online relationship building process can be a powerful mechanism for building trust and for developing a long-term relationship between online partners.
trust is an important factor in interorganizational relationships, and that the role of institutional trust can be used to complement and substitute the role of familiarity in online relationships.
institutional trust is necessary for online relationship building, and that it can substitute for familiarity, and then complement it, in the initial phases of the online relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that
institutional trust is an effective mechanism to build interorganizational trust in the online context, especially in the early stages of the relationship, when familiarity is still limited.

the role of third-party institutions in trust formation is not limited to the initial stages of online relationships, as it also plays a role in the subsequent phases of online inter-organizational relationship building.
the role of institutional trust is time-dependent and that it progressively shifts its role from that of a substitute for to a complement of familiarity.
